children.title: Expert Practice
children.html: Select your Expert Practice from those listed at the end of the class description. Your Practice is the career that gave you the majority of your skills. It grants you facets when you select it, and again at 4th, 7th, and 10th level.

children.title: Expert Maneuvers
children.html:
Your varied skillset allows you to execute Instinctual and Tactical maneuvers by spending Stamina. You start with a maximum of 3 Stamina, and your maximum increases each level, as shown in the Stamina column of the Expert Class Table. When you execute a maneuver, you must spend Stamina equal to the maneuver’s level. You regain expended Stamina when you finish a Rest.

Choose two 1st-level maneuvers of the types you can learn (Instinctual and Tactical) as your initial maneuvers. You learn an additional maneuver each level as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the Expert Class Table. The maximum maneuver level you're allowed to learn is shown in the Max Maneuver Level column on that table as well.

children.title: Expertise
Highly Skilled
children.html: Any Skill Check you make using the Mod Die of a Hobby or Profession is Bolstered with a level equal to half your Expert Bonus.

children.title: Additional Hobbies
children.html: You gain two additional Hobbies at Amateur Rank. You gain another Hobby at Amateur Rank time your Expert Bonus increases.

children.title: Expert's Tools
children.html:
An Expert always has their tools on hand. Your Expert’s Tools allow you to make any Check involving one of your Hobbies or Professions that would normally require portable tools as if you had them.

Choose one type of Light weapon, one type of Close-Up weapon, and one type of Precise weapon. The chosen weapons become part of your Expert’s Tools. When you Strike, you can use a weapon of any type on your person designated as part of your Expert’s Tools without having to Interact to draw it or stow a different weapon.

You can change your chosen weapon types each time you gain a level.

children.title: Adroit Strikes
children.html:
You can leverage your array of skills to attack with precision. Once per turn when you Strike a creature, you can replace the Mod Die of the Attack Check with your Tactical Die. To do so, one of the below conditions must be met.

  • Advantage. You have Advantage on the Attack Check.

  • Distracted. There is an Ally within 1 space of the target that has at least 1 remaining and is not Unconscious.

  • Focused. You spent at least 3 on the Strike (not including CAP).

For that Attack Check, add your Expert Bonus to the DV of your weapon, and add twice that to the Deadly DV.

children.html: You’ve spent your life sharpening your skills to a fine edge, granting you the facets below.

Choose one of your Hobbies or Professions. The triggering Check is rolled in Tandem with the Mod Die of the chosen Hobby or Profession.

You can Evaluate with each of your Hobbies once per Long Rest. You can Evaluate with each of your Professions once per Short Rest.

children.html: Using your vast experience, you can prepare unorthodox ways to overcome challenges. You gain the Evaluate reaction, described below.

children.title: Superior Tactics
Reposition
children.html: You quickly assess your surroundings for the best positioning. Stepping and Taking Cover cost 1 for you.

children.title: Plot
children.html: You see your opponents' moves before they do. On your turn, you can spend all of your remaining . You can then spend 1 to take a Reaction at any point before you next turn. When you do, you gain temporary equal to the spent and can take any number of Actions in a row. Any unspent temporary disappears when you finish taking Actions.

children.title: Retort
children.html: You respond to new situations at a moments notice. At the end of your turn, you can state a Trigger as if you were Preparing an action. If the Trigger occurs, you can take any Action with a base cost of 2 or less as if it were a Reaction in response to the Trigger.
Choose your preferred approach to solving dangerous problems from those listed below. At 5th and 8th level, you will gain additional abilities based on your choice.
Jack of all trades and master of several, Experts leverage their extensive experience to great effect.

children.title: Expert Practices
Investigator
Professional Investigator
children.html: You gain the Investigator Profession at Proficient Rank, or a Profession of your choice if you already have it.

children.title: Investigator’s Tools
children.html: Choose one type of Ranged weapon that lacks the Heavy and Massive properties. You can wield weapons of the chosen type, and they become part of your Expert’s Tools. The short range of thrown and ranged weapons in your Expert’s Tools is equal to your Radius if it would be lower.

children.title: Eagle-Eyed
children.html:
Searching and Detecting cost 1 for you, and your Attribute Checks are rolled in Tandem with your Tactical Die.

When you Strike, you can spend an additional 1 to Search for something on the target as part of the same Action, rolling your Attack Check before the PM rolls your Check. If your Strike is a Success, you have Advantage on the Secret Check.
With eyes like a knife and a brain bright as the Sun at Apex, Investigators don't let nothin' slip. Best mind your P's and Q's, if you know what's good for ya.
In everything we do, there's always someone better. The Expert is that someone. An Expert's Practice is their arena, in which their skills are unmatched.

children.html: Select your Martial Training from those listed at the end of the class description. Your Martial Training is the lessons of the people and places that turned you into a Gladiator. It grants you facets when you select it, and again at 4th, 7th, and 10th level.

children.title: Martial Maneuvers
children.html:
Your path as a Gladiator allows you to execute maneuvers by spending Stamina. You start with a maximum of 3 Stamina, and your maximum increases each level, as shown in the Stamina column of the Gladiator Class Table. When you execute a maneuver, you must spend Stamina equal to the maneuver’s level. You regain expended Stamina when you finish a Rest.

Choose three 1st-level maneuvers of the types you can learn as determined by your Martial Training for your initial maneuvers. You learn additional maneuvers each level as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the Gladiator Class Table. The maximum maneuver level you're allowed to learn is shown in the Max Maneuver Level column on that table as well.

children.html: As a trained fighter, you have exceptional combat prowess and intuition. You gain the Reignite and Size Up Actions, described below.

children.title: Action Flare
children.html:
On your turn, you can choose to gain temporary equal to your Gladiator Bonus. When you do, you regain expended Stamina equal to half your Gladiator Bonus, and the CAP for all of your Actions resets. Any unspent temporary disappears at the end of your turn.

Once you use this facet, you must finish a Rest before you can do so again. You gain an additional use of this facet between Rests at 8th level.

children.title: Combat Style
children.html: Choose your preferred style of fighting, known as your Combat Style from those listed after the Class description. You become Adept in that Combat Style. When you reach 5th and 8th level, you can choose to gain a new one, or progress with a previously chosen Style, becoming Expert, then Master.

children.title: Combat Styles
Archery
children.html:
The thrum of a loosed drawstring never sounded so deadly as yours.

Adept You can roll your Die in Tandem with your Martial Die when you make an Attack Check with a Drawn weapon.

children.title: Defensive Fighting
children.html:
The best offense is a good defense.

Adept The first time you make an Attack Check on each of your turns, you can choose to have that Attack Check and all others you make on that turn be Hindered 1. If you do, you gain a bonus to your AC equal to half your Gladiator Bonus until the beginning of your next turn.

children.title: Dueling
children.html:
A proper duelist uses many forms.

Adept When you make an Attack Check with a Versatile weapon while wielding it with two hands, the Deadly DV increases by 1. When you Strike with a Versatile weapon while wielding it with one hand, you can Seize or Shove as part of that Action by spending an additional 1 , before or after your Attack Check.

children.title: Fencer
children.html:
You prefer your blades to be lithe and swift.

Adept You can roll your Die in Tandem with your Martial Die when you make an Attack Check with a Deft weapon.

children.title: Greatweapon Fighting
children.html:
You specialize in wielding great hunks of steel that most would hesitate to call weapons.

Adept Attack Checks you make with Massive weapons are Bolstered 1.

children.title: Heavy Weapon Fighting
children.html:
You favor true weapons of war that take both hands to master.

Adept You can roll your Die in Tandem with your Martial Die when you make an Attack Check with a Heavy melee weapon.

children.title: Juggernaut
children.html:
You have the strength to wield larger weapons with ease.

Adept You can ignore the Two-Handed property for Heavy weapons you wield.
Gladiators are adept with all forms of weaponry, but they still have their favorites. The Combat Styles available to a Gladiator are described below.
Masters of weaponry in all forms and trained to fight until they drop, gladiators are masters of the battlefield.

children.title: Martial Trainings
Victor
Surge to Victory
children.html:
You can learn Feral, Martial, and Instinctual maneuvers.

Once per Rest, you can execute one of your maneuvers at your Max Maneuver Level without expending Stamina.

children.title: Practiced Combatant
children.html: Your Attack Checks score a Critical Success when you roll a 19 or 20 on the d20. You can also Step immediately after you score a Critical Success on an Attack Check without spending any .

children.title: Peerless Athlete
children.html:
Your dedication to maintaining your physique grants you the benefits below.

  • Your Initiative Checks and Attribute Checks are rolled in Tandem with your Martial Die.

  • Your Basic Skill Checks are Bolstered 1.

  • Your Save Checks are Empowered.
To the victor go the spoils, and there is no greater spoil than victory itself. You have and continue to train tirelessly, ever pushing yourself to be the greatest.
Each Gladiator is forged from the methods and environments that taught them the skills to succeed in combat. Their Training keeps them tuned to the rhythm of battle where others would be overwhelmed.

Select your Primordial Soul from those listed at the end of the class description. Your Primordial Soul is the ancient creature with which you share your soul. It grants you facets when you select it, and again at 2nd, 4th, 7th, and 10th level.

Your Primordial Soul will allow you to cast certain spells, using the Channel Action, described below.

children.title: Incarnate Maneuvers
children.html:
Your enhanced senses allow you to execute Feral and Instinctual maneuvers by spending Stamina. You start with a maximum of 3 Stamina, and your maximum increases each level, as shown in the Stamina column of the Incarnate Class Table. When you execute a maneuver, you must spend Stamina equal to the maneuver’s level. You regain expended Stamina when you finish a Rest.

Choose two 1st-level maneuvers of the types you can learn (Feral and Instinctual) as your initial maneuvers. You learn an additional maneuver each level as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the Incarnate Class Table. The maximum maneuver level you're allowed to learn is shown in the Max Maneuver Level column on that table as well.

Ferocious Strikes
children.html: You can replace your Die with your Primordial Die when you Unarmed Strike (it's still a Check). If you do, the DV equals half your Incarnate Bonus, and the Deadly DV is your Incarnate Bonus.

children.title: Primeval Force
children.html: The first time on each of your turns that you make a Successful Unarmed Strike, you deal additional Sonic damage to the target and gain Temporary Endurance equal to your Points.

children.title: Primal Reflexes
children.html: When you roll Initiative, you can Stride as a Reaction. If you do, your Initiative Check is rolled in Tandem with your Primordial Die.
The primeval savagery of your primordial grants you the facets below.

children.title: Manifestations
children.html:
Features of your Primordial have begun to appear on your body, granting you supernatural ability. Choose an Attribute for your Manifestations to improve. You gain the first tier of benefits for that Attribute as listed after the Class description.

Every even level after this one, you choose an Attribute again, gaining the next tier of benefits if you’ve selected it before.

Each Manifestation you gain causes a noticeable physical change of your choice on your body, reflective of your Primordial Soul.

Categories

Cost

Requirements
You have enough unoccupied adjacent spaces to increase your Size; You haven't Titan Morphed since your last Long Rest.

Spend any amount of up to your Max Maneuver Level. You enter your Titanus Form, the benefits of which are described in your Primordial Soul. During your Titanus Form, your Size increases based on the amount of you spent, as shown in the table below.

AP Size
1 Gigantic
2 Enormous
3 Gargantuan
4 Colossal
5 Titanic

The amount of you spent becomes your Size Bonus for the duration of your Titanus Form, which affects you in the ways below.

  • Checks. Your and Checks are Bolstered with a level equal to your Size Bonus.

  • Movement. Your Movement increases by your Size Bonus.

  • Reach. Your Melee Attack Checks can reach targets an additional number of spaces away from you equal to your Size Bonus.

  • Resistance. You have Crushing, Piercing, and Slashing Resistance equal to twice your Size Bonus.

  • Stamina. You regain spent Stamina equal to your Size Bonus at the end of your turn.

  • Temporary Endurance. When you Titan Morph, you gain Temporary Endurance equal to 10 times your Size Bonus.

During your Titanus Form, any equipment you are wearing becomes unusable, and you are unarmored. You remain in your Titanus Form for 1 minute, and it only ends early if you die.

Ancient lord of ice and beast from before the dominion of gods, the King ruled as the strongest Primordial, keeping order through force. Through your connected souls, you feel the chilling might of an endless iceberg.

Pagan apocrypha and raving zealots tell the stories of ancient titans. Creatures that roamed the Prism before even the gods, supposedly. Incarnates give more weight to those stories than Prismatic adherents are comfortable with.

Spells Prepared this way must have a level no higher than your Max Favor, as shown in the Thaumaturge Class Table.

  • Bolstered Save. The first Save Check you make before your next turn is Bolstered 1.

  • Hindered Attack. The first Attack Check made against you before your next turn is Hindered 1.

You become aware of supernatural afflictions within your Radius for 10 minutes. During that time, objects, areas, and creatures with supernatural afflictions or that hide objects with such afflictions glow faintly to you. You can spend 2 to take the Identify Supernatural action against them as long as they are within your Radius. You cannot Detect Supernatural through 1 inch of metal, 1 foot of stone, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

As a divinely ordained minister of your deity, you can perform rites to identify the presence of supernatural forces. When you Identify Supernatural, the PM rolls your Miracle Die in Tandem with your Die for the Secret Check, which is Empowered. You also gain the Detect Supernatural Action, described below.

children.html: A devout and proven follower, your deity grants you special attention. You gain the Entreat Miracle Action, described below.

children.title: Entreating Prayer
children.html: When you Pray during an Encounter, you can choose to spend an additional 1 to shout your prayer as loud as you can, giving that Prayer the Spoken requirement. If you do, you can roll your Die in Tandem with your Miracle Die for any Check made as part of Evoking a spell that turn. Your Indebted level then increases by 2 after Evoking it.
Miracle workers both benevolent and destructive, Thaumaturges are the most prominent conduits of divine will.

children.title: Divine Domains
Cosmos Domain
Domain Spells
children.html:
As a Thaumaturge of the cosmos, you can Prepare Frost, Pneuma, Lunar, and Platinum evocations with your Thaumaturgy feature, as well as Mind and Moon arcana.

You also learn three mantras, each of which must be either Frost, Pneuma, Lunar, or Platinum. You can choose to learn a Mind or Moon cantrip in place of any number of these mantras.

children.title: Guiding Moonlight
children.html: When you make an Attribute Check, it is Bolstered with a level equal to half your Thaumaturge Bonus.

children.title: Cosmic Knowledge
children.html:
Once per turn after you deal Cosmic damage, you can roll your Die in Tandem with your Miracle Die. You gain Temporary Endurance equal to the result.

Also, when you would deal Psychic damage, you can choose to deal Cosmic damage instead.

children.title: Lunar Miracle
Reveal Secrets
children.html:
For 1 minute, Moonlight fills the area around you in an emanation with a size equal to your Thaumaturge Bonus plus 1. Any Skill Checks made by you or an Ally within the emanation are Bolstered 1, and any Hostile Invisible creatures and objects within it glow with blue light.

Anything within the emanation that was made or altered to have a secret meaning, including text, iconography, pictures, or objects, glows blue. For example, the text of an innocuous letter that is actually coded language would glow, however nothing about the true meaning of the text is revealed.
When you Entreat a Miracle, you can choose the Reveal Secrets option, described below.

For eons, denizens of the facets have whispered of the secrets held within the Moon. They say praying to the its master, Lunaeus, god of knowledge and trickery, can bring great wisdom. Sometimes, too great.

Thaumaturges are made from the most devout followers of the deities that make up the Prismatic Pantheon. The abilities of a Thaumaturge depend on the Divine Domain of their god, which describe their sphere of influence over the Prismos.

fields.Skill Checks: When you make a Basic Skill Check with your {PRS} and Art Die in Tandem, it is Empowered.
fields.Spells: Your {PRS} Die is your Spell Mod Die. Checks you make with your Spell Mod Die count as {PRS} Checks.
fields.Weapons: You can wield any weapon that isn’t a melee weapon with the Two-Handed property.

children.title: Artistic Medium
children.html: Select your Artistic Medium from those listed at the end of the class description. Your Artistic Medium is the method through which you create. Your Artistic Medium grants you facets when you select it, and again at 4th, 7th, and 10th level.

children.title: Favored Genre
children.html:
Every artist has their preference, a style that deeply influences their work. Choose your Favored Genre from those listed after the class description. You gain benefits based on your choice, and you gain additional benefits at 5th and 8th level.

Each time you gain a Troubadour level, you swap your Favored Genre.

children.title: Artist’s Light
Confound
children.html:
Categories
Supernatural, Move, Hostile
Cost
Reaction, 2 , Basic CAP
Trigger
A Hostile creature within your Radius that can sense you makes a Check.

Distracting the creature with a mocking display, you roll your Art Die and subtract it from the result of the triggering Check. If you aren’t Prone and have at least 2 Movement, you can also move a number of spaces up to your Points.

You can Confound a number of times equal to your Points plus 1 (minimum 1). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Rest.

fields.Trigger: A Hostile creature within your {PER} Radius that can sense you makes a Check.

children.title: Inspire
children.html:
Categories
Supernatural, Move
Cost
Reaction, 2 , Basic CAP
Trigger
An Ally within your Radius that can sense you makes a Check.

Using your talents to create a moment of beauty, the Ally gains Temporary Endurance equal to your Points and may roll the triggering Check in Tandem with your Art Die. If you aren’t Prone and have at least 2 Movement, you can also move a number of spaces up to your Points.

You can Inspire a number of times equal to your Points plus 1 (minimum 1). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Rest.

fields.Trigger: An Ally within your {PER} Radius that can sense you makes a Check.

children.html: As a practitioner of the arts, you can inspire rage and awe in equal measure. You gain the Confound and Inspire Actions, described below.

children.title: Practice Drills
children.html: Mastery of the basics is essential to any craft. You can spend 10 minutes doing practice drills to keep your mind sharp. Afterward, you gain a number of temporary Radiance equal to half your Troubadour Bonus that last until you finish a Rest. Once you use this facet, you must finish a Rest before you can use it again.

children.title: Wondercraft
Preparing spells
children.html: Each Long Rest, you can Prepare a number of spells equal to your Troubadour Bonus plus your Points, allowing you to cast those spells until your next Long Rest. Spells Prepared this way must have a level no higher than your Max Spell Level, as shown in the Troubadour Class Table. The types of spells you can Prepare are determined by your Favored Genre.

children.title: Casting Spells
Evoke Wonder
children.html:
Categories
Supernatural, Concentrate, Move, Hostile
Cost
Wonder, in spell’s Cast Time
Requirements
You haven’t Evoked Wonder this turn

You create art to cast one of your mantras or Prepared evocations at a level up to your Max Spell Level.

fields.Requirements: You haven’t Evoked Wonder this turn

children.html: Through your Artistic Medium, you create art, and the Prismos reacts. You gain the Evoke Wonder action, described below.

Your art is so powerful it moves the world to imitate, allowing you to cast spells from the Wonder you create. You start with a maximum of 2 Wonder, and your maximum increases at certain Troubadour Levels, as shown in the Wonder column of the Troubadour Class Table. You regain expended Wonder when you finish a Rest.
Masters of the arts, Troubadours rouse the world with beauty beyond measure, evoking wonder with their craft.

children.title: Favored Genres
Comedy
children.html:
There is no ailment not somewhat lessened by a laugh.

1st Level When you Inspire a creature, the Temporary Endurance it gains increases by twice your Troubadour Bonus.

You also gain a level of Lunar Alignment.

2nd Level You can Prepare Flame, Pneuma, Mordant, Lunar, and Platinum Evocations.

children.title: Tragedy
children.html:
Through sorrow, we are reminded what is truly important.

1st Level When you Confound a creature, it is Numbed 1 for 1 minute.

You also gain a level of Pneuma Alignment.

2nd Level You can Prepare Pneuma, Velvet, Infernal, Lunar, and Platinum Evocations.

children.title: Romance
children.html:
There is nothing so intoxicating as the scent of blooming love.

1st Level When you Inspire a creature, any player not playing the create may choose to spend one of their Radiance on the triggering Check. If they do, they gain Temporary Endurance equal to twice your Points.

You also gain a level of Velvet Alignment.

2nd Level You can Prepare Flame, Frost, Soma, Velvet, and Platinum Evocations.
To create is to feel. Your Favored Genre represents those feelings you resonant with most strongly.

children.title: Artistic Mediums
Dance
Stagework
children.html:
The Prismos itself becomes your stage crew, causing thin strings of Platinum Light to hoist you and your props. When you throw a Thrown weapon as part of an Attack Check, the weapon returns to you immediately afterward, so long as the target was within your Radius.

You can also move in any direction while Jumping, instead of only a straight line. When you fall, subtract your Troubadour Bonus from the number of spaces you fell before calculating damage.

children.title: Dance Partner
children.html: When you end your turn in a space adjacent to an Ally, if you took a Move Action that turn they become your Dance Partner until the start of your turn. Once before then, you can Inspire one of your Dance Partner's Attack Checks without expending a use, and doing so only costs 1 .
Mobile masters of the stage, Troubadours of Dance weave through battle like they been rehearsing for years.
Few things move a crowd to action like a well timed art piece. The Artistic Medium of a Troubadour is platform from which they change the Prism.

children.title: Weapon Properties
Ammo
children.html: Making an Attack Check with an Ammo weapon requires one piece of the ammunition listed in the property.

children.title: Blocking
children.html: While wielding a Blocking weapon, your AC increases by 1 if it’s Heavy, or 2 if it’s Massive. Blocking weapons are required to Block.

children.title: Bludgeoning
children.html: When you make an Attack Check with a Bludgeoning weapon, the target takes damage equal to the weapon's DV or the value of your Mod Die on a Failure, whichever is higher.

children.title: Brutal
children.html: When you make an Attack Check with a Brutal weapon, you can spend any amount of additional . The Check Total is reduced by that amount, the weapon's DV increases by three time that amount, and its Deadly DV increases by four times that amount.

children.title: Close-up
children.html: When you make a Melee Attack Check with a Close-up weapon, you can spend an additional 1 to Step, before or after making the Attack Check. You can’t make Attack Checks with Close-up weapons while Immobilized, unless the target is touching you.

children.title: Deft
children.html: You can use instead of for Attack Checks made with Deft weapons, which have lower DVs but higher Deadly DVs. Wielding a Deft weapon requires at least 2 Points.

children.title: Drawn (X - Y)
children.html:
When you take an Action to make an Attack Check with a Drawn weapon, you spend any amount of listed in the range of the property, instead of the normal amount for that Action. The minimum you must spend is the amount normally required by the Action you’re taking, but for every spent beyond the minimum, the below effects apply to your Attack Check.

  • The weapon’s Deadly DV increases by 1.

  • The value of your Mod Die increases by 1.

  • The weapon’s short range increases by 2 spaces.

You cannot make Reaction Strikes with Drawn weapons, and you have Disadvantage on Weapon Attack Checks with them if there is a Hostile creature within 1 space of you.

children.title: Heavy
children.html: Wielding a Heavy weapon requires at least 2 Points.

children.title: Light
children.html: When you Strike with a Light weapon during your turn, you can reduce the cost of that Action by 1. You can do so once on each of your turns for each Light weapon you are wielding, but you can only use the Light property of one weapon per Action. Each time you do, your AC is reduced by 1 until the start of your next turn.

children.title: Massive
children.html: Any Action you take involving an Attack Check with a Massive weapon costs an additional 1 . Wielding a Massive weapon also reduces your Movement by 2 spaces, and you can’t make Attack Checks with Massive weapons if you have less than 3 Points.

children.title: Nonlethal
children.html: Creatures reduced to 0 Endurance from damage dealt with a Nonlethal weapon do not die or lose Vitality. non-PC creatures are still knocked Unconscious.

children.title: Precise
children.html: You can use instead of for Attack Checks made with Precise weapons, whose Deadly DV equals the weapon’s DV or the value rolled on your Mod Die, whichever is higher. When you make an Attack Check with a Precise weapon, you can spend any amount of additional . For that Attack Check, the value of your Mod Die increases by the additional spent. Wielding a Precise weapon requires at least 2 Points.

children.title: Pulling
children.html:
Once per turn, when you make a Successful Attack Check with a Pulling weapon, you can have the target make a or Save (their choice) against your Check Total.

Failure
You move them 1 space to an unoccupied space adjacent to you.
Deadly Failure
As a Failure, Prone.

If your Attack Check was a Deadly Success, the Save Check gains the below additional effects.

Failure
The target drops one object they are holding.
Deadly Failure
You can catch the dropped object (no required).

fields.Failure: The target drops one object they are holding.
fields.Deadly Failure: You can catch the dropped object (no {AP} required).

children.title: Puncturing
children.html: Piercing damage dealt by Puncturing weapons ignores Piercing resistance granted by armor.

children.title: Pushing
children.html:
Once per turn, when you make a Successful Attack Check with a Pushing weapon while you are not Immobilized, you can have the target make a or Save (their choice) against your Check Total.

Failure
Buffeted 1.
Deadly Failure
Buffeted 2 or Prone (your choice).

fields.Deadly Failure: Buffeted 2 or Prone (your choice).

children.title: Ranged
children.html: Striking with a Ranged weapon has a basic CAP. When you make an Attack Check with a Ranged weapon, you must use instead of . If the target is not within a number of spaces equal to the first number listed in the property, the Attack Check has Disadvantage. You cannot target anything beyond the second listed number of spaces. Wielding a Ranged weapon requires at least 2 Points.

children.title: Reach
children.html: When you make an Attack Check with a Reach weapon, your target can be an additional space away from you.

children.title: Reload
children.html: After making an Attack Check with a Reload weapon, you can't do so again until you spend the listed in the property to load a piece of ammunition into the weapon. Reloading a weapon is a Move and Manipulate Action.

children.title: Simple
children.html: Simple weapons don't need training to wield.

children.title: Sparklock
children.html: Making an Attack Check with a Sparklock weapon creates a thunderous sound audible out to 60 spaces, and requires 1g of Powdered Citrine per Attack Check.

children.title: Thrown
children.html: When you make an Attack Check with a Thrown weapon, you can choose to throw it, rolling either your or Die in Tandem with your Mod Die for that Attack Check. If the target is not within a number of spaces equal to the first number listed in the property, the Attack Check has Disadvantage. You cannot target anything beyond the second listed number of spaces.

children.title: Two-handed
children.html: Wielding a Two-handed weapon requires two hands to be on the weapon while making an Attack Check.

children.title: Versatile
children.html: You can wield a Versatile weapon with one hand or two. When wielded with two hands, use the DVs listed in parentheses.
Weapon properties drastically affect how a weapon is used. Take time to understand the properties of your chosen weapon and how you can use them to your advantage.

Listed in the table below are the details of all weapons available to PCs. Each row lists the weapon's name and the following information.

Damage Value (DV). The amount of damage dealt by the weapon on a Weapon Attack Check Success.

Deadly Damage Value (Deadly DV). The amount of damage dealt by the weapon on a Weapon Attack Check Deadly Success. A value of "Mod Die" means the Deadly DV equals the weapon's DV or the value rolled on your Mod Die for the Attack Check, whichever is higher.

Damage Type. The type or types of damage the weapon can deal. If multiple types are listed, you choose one each time you make a Successful Attack Check with the weapon.

Requirements. The Attribute Points required to properly wield the weapon. You have Disadvantage on any Weapon Attack Check you make with a weapon for which you don’t meet the listed requirements, or do not have the proper training to wield.

Properties. Properties affect how a weapon is used, and are defined below the table.

children.title: Armor
Light Armor
children.html: Your AC gains a bonus equal to your Points.

children.title: Medium Armor
children.html:
Your AC gains a bonus equal to your Points.

Resistance You gain Slashing Resistance equal to half the armor’s AC value.

Weighty Your Save Checks are Hindered 1.

children.title: Heavy Armor
children.html:
Your AC gains a bonus equal to your Points.

Resistance You gain Slashing Resistance equal to your armor’s AC value and half as much Piercing Resistance.

Restricted Movement You Movement is reduced by 1 space and your Mod Die is reduced in size by one step.

Heavy Standing costs 2 .

children.title: Armor Requirements
children.html:
Armor has an amount of Points required to wear it effectively. If you don’t meet the Point requirement of armor you are wearing, all Checks you make are Weakened.

There are three types of armor in BtP: Light, Medium, and Heavy. Each has different effects when worn, described below.

children.title: Bulk
children.html:
An object’s Bulk Rank measures how many of that object you can stow on your person. If an object has Bulk 1, you can only carry one of that item in your inventory. If an object has Bulk 2, you can only carry two of them, and so on to Bulk 5. Objects with Bulk 0 can’t be stowed on your person and must be carried with both hands. If an object has no Bulk, you can carry any number of them, subject to common sense.

Items of lower Bulk Rank can take up your inventory for items of higher Bulk Rank. For example, you could have three Bulk 2 items on your person, but if you do, you can’t stow a Bulk 1 item, as you can’t take up lower rank slots with a Bulk 1 item.

For each Point you have, you unlock additional inventory slots matching that number of points. So with 1 Point, you can carry an additional Bulk 1 item. With 2, you can carry two additional Bulk 2 items.

children.title: {SL} Level
children.titleHtml: Level
children.html:
Level is listed after type, below the name. The symbol means to use the spell or maneuver's level. When you see a number beside the symbol, for example "2", that equals the level multiplied by 2. Numbers are also sometimes added to the level, for example " plus 1".

A creature that suffers a Failure against a Fire Spout spell will take 3 plus 2 Thermic damage. This means cast at 1st level, Fire Spout will deal (3 * 1) + 2 = 5 Thermic damage. At 2nd level, it will deal (3 * 2) + 2 = 8 Thermic damage.

children.title: Type
Arcanum Spell Types
children.html: The arcanum spell types are Fire, Ice, Mind, Bio, Scour, Arc, Blood, Moon, World, and Null. Creatures that draw light from within themselves are typically able to cast these spells.

children.title: Evocation Spell Types
children.html: The evocation spell types are Flame, Frost, Pneuma, Soma, Mordant, Velvet, Infernal, Lunar, Temporal, and Platinum. Creatures that wield light from external sources, such as dieties, are able to cast these spells.

children.title: Maneuver Types
children.html: The maneuver types are Feral, Martial, Instinctual, Tactical, and Psychological. Each of these types corresponds with an Attribute.
Each spell and maneuver has a type that determines whether your PC can learn it based off their facets.

children.title: Cast & Execution Time
Trigger
children.html: Reaction spells and maneuvers will list their trigger, which is the circumstance upon which you can use them. You can only take one Action in response to any single trigger.

The cast or execution time of most spells and maneuvers is measured in . Spells with longer cast times measured in minutes can't be cast in a single turn, requiring 5 every 5 seconds (each round of an Encounter) until the listed cast time has passed. Maneuvers with an execution time of Strike are done as part of the Strike Action.

Spells are cast as part of a separate Action, while Maneuvers with a cost time measured in are considered Concentrate Actions.

children.title: Range
children.html:
Range is the effective area of a spell or maneuver. Most will measure their range in spaces, meaning the target can be no more than the listed spaces away from the creature using it. Many spells and maneuvers will also list an area of effect (see the Areas of Effect section for more details). Some special ranges are listed below.

Touch
means the user must be able to physically touch the target.
Self
will either only affect you, or will originiate from you if an area of effect is also listed.
Vocal
can target any creature that can hear you.
Strike Range
means within range of the weapon you are wielding.

fields.Touch: means the user must be able to physically touch the target.
fields.Self: will either only affect you, or will originiate from you if an area of effect is also listed.
fields.Vocal: can target any creature that can hear you.
fields.Strike Range: means within range of the weapon you are wielding.

children.title: Components & requirements
Hands
children.html: One or two hands mean you must have that many hands free in order to cast the spell.

children.title: Spoken
children.html: A Spoken requirement mean you must vocalize some part of the action. If you can't speak, you can't use spells or maneuvers with a Spoken requirement.

children.title: Charged Gemstones
children.html: Some arcane spells require an amount of charge from a charged gemstone measured in grams (g). You must be holding the gemstone as you cast the spell, but the hand(s) used to hold it count as free for Hand requirements. After casting a spell with such a requirement, that much charge is depleted from the gemstone.

children.title: Powdered Gemstones
children.html: Some arcane spells require an amount of powdered gemstone, measured in grams (g). You must have the powdered gemstone in hand as you cast the spell, but the hand(s) used to hold it count as free for Hand requirements. After casting a spell with such a requirement, that much powdered gemstone is consumed.
Most spells and maneuvers have one more components or requirements, some common ones are described below, but requirements can be many things.

children.title: Duration
Sustained
children.html: Spells and maneuvers that list Sustained before their duration require you to take the Sustain Action on each of your turns to maintain the effect. If you don't, the effect ends at the end of your turn.

Duration explains how long the effect lasts. An Instant duration means the effect is performed upon use and is usually done afterward. A duration of 1 or more minutes creates a continuous effect that ends after the listed duration.

children.title: Exalted
Note on Mod Dice
children.html:
When a spell or maneuver requires you to make a Check, your Mod Die for the Check is your Spell or Maneuver Mod Die, unless otherwise stated. Your class will tell you what kind of Attribute Check your Spell Checks are considered (typically or ). A Maneuver Checks Attribute depends on its type, such as DC Checks for a Feral Maneuver counting as .

This is important, because if you are Numbed 1 and you try to execute an Instinctual Maneuver, your Mod Die for Checks made as part of that maneuver will be reduced in size one step. An Arcanist that is Muddled 1 will similarly have their Spell Mod Die reduced for any Checks they make for their spells.

Exalted effects alter the way the spell or maneuver performs when used at higher levels. Exalted (+1) effects are applied once for each level above the base (listed) level. Exalted (+2) effects are applied once for every two levels above the base. Exalted effects that list a specific level are applied when the spell or maneuver is used at that level, in order from lowest to highest.

Traits
children.html:
Familiar The familiar is under your command using the following rules.

  • PM Control. The PM controls the familiar, but you roll its Checks.

  • Maximum. The familiar’s Maximum is 3.

  • Initiative. If summoned during an encounter, it shares your Initiative and takes its turn after yours.

  • Nonverbal. The familiar can’t speak, but has an arcane understanding of any verbal commands you give it (no required), and will follow them to the best of its ability.

Ethereal
The familiar can’t physically interact with creatures or objects, takes no damage from falling, and any Crushing, Piercing, or Slashing damage it takes is halved. When it Jumps, it can move up to half its Movement vertically or horizontally, instead of the normal amount of spaces.
Perfect Memory
The familiar remembers everything it hears and sees after your initial summoning. Even if it dies, it retains all memories it has from being in your service.
Telepathic Bond
The familiar can psychically relay information to you while you are within its Radius times . The information it can relay is based on the level of this spell:

  • 1st level and up It can relay words and sounds.

  • 2nd level and up It can project still images of things it has seen.

  • 4th level and up It can project any memory it has acquired while summoned by you.

  • 5th level You can speak to the familiar telepathically while within range of its Telepathic Bond.

Cast Time

1 space

Extracting Mind Prisma from the Charged Spinel, you summon a spirit familiar resembling the ghostly apparition of a tiny creature of your choice. Each time you cast this spell, you can re-summon the same spirit, or release the previous spirit from your service and summon a new one.

During your turn, if you can sense your familiar, you can spend 1 absorb it into a 2g uncharged spinel that you are holding. While contained within the spinel, you can spend 1 during your turn to release it in an unoccupied space adjacent to you.

Your familiar uses the stat block on the next page.

  • Overdrive. When the target makes a , , or Save or Skill Check, the Check is Bolstered 1. Any Temporary Endurance remaining after the Check resolves is sacrificed.

  • Illusory Mimicry. You take Actions and move as the duplicate. But any Action that would interact physically with the world or deal any damage except Cosmic has no effect outside of being a visible illusion.

  • Sensory Relay. You experience nothing in your body, but sense from the duplicate as though it were you.

children.title: Glossary
children.html:
AP
(Stands for Action Point) Resource used to perform actions, regained at the end of a creatures turn.
Advantage
Modifies Checks by having the rolling entity roll an additional d20, taking the higher value between the d20s for the Check total.
AGI
(Stands for Agility) Measure of how fast a creature can move.
Ancestry
A PC's creature type chosen durning character creation.
Arcane
Descriptor of mystical effects created with intentby sapient effort.
Arcanum
Type of spell cast with personal talent.
Attack Check
Check made when a creature attempts to harm something in a way that requires accuracy.
Attribute
The measures of a creature's capability; Vigor, Agility, Perception, Intelligence, Presence.
Attribute Check
Skill Check made to do something simple; abberviated as -Attribute- Check (e.g. Check).
Attribute Points
Measure of the potency of a given creature's attribute; abbreviated as Points, Points, etc.
Basic Skill Check
Skill Check made to do something that requires basic knowledge of the task; always two Attributes rolled in Tandem. Abbreviated as "Tandem 'Attr.' / 'Attr.' Check", or simply "'Attr.' / 'Attr. Check'" (e.g. "Make a / Check").
Bolstered X
Modifies Checks by increasing the size of the largest Mod Die by one step for each level (e.g., from a d6 to a d8).
BtP
(Stands for Beyond the Prism) The name of this ttrpg.
Check
The act of rolling a d20; includes Attack Checks, Save Checks, and Skill Checks.
Check Total
The final result of a Check, compared against the DC.
Class
Description of a PC's capabilities, gained through great dedication or natural talent.
DC
(Stands for Difficulty Class) Number that a Check Total must meet or exceed for Success.
DC Check
Special Check made by rolling a Mod Die and adding 10.
Disadvantage
Modifies Checks by having the rolling entity roll an additional d20, taking the lower value between the d20s for the Check total.
Empowered
Modifies Checks by either having a Tandem check add both Mod Dice to the Check total, or adding 1d4 to the Check total if one of the Mod Dice is a d2 or smaller.
Endurance
Resource that represnts a creatures ability to function under high-stress situations. Damage is subtracted from Endurance.
Evocation
Type of spell cast by borrowing power.
Facet
A feature of a PC, comes from many sources.
Hindered X
Modifies Checks by reducing the size of the largest Mod Die by one step for each level (e.g., from a d4 to a d2).
Hobby
An activity a PC had experience in before they became an adventurer; allows a PC to make Trained Skill Checks related to them.
INT
(Stands for Intelligence) Measure of how smart a creature is.
Maneuver
Technique requiring great physical or mental skill.
Mod Die
(Stands for Modifer Die) A die rolled with a d20 when making a Check; often shorthanded to -Attribute- Die (e.g., Die).
PER
(Stands for Perception) Measure of how well a creature utilizes its senses.
PC
(Stands for Player Character) A creature controlled by one of the players during a session.
PM
(Stands for Prism Master) The game master; they control everything in the story apart from PCs.
Profession
A PC's occupation before they became an adventurer; allows a PC to make money during Downtime and make Trained Skill Checks related to them.
PRS
(Stands for Presence) Measure of how influential a creature is.
Radiance
Resource that allows a creature to improve any Check they make by expending it.
Save Check
Check made when a creature attempts to avoid something harmful.
Skill Check
Check made when a creature tries to affect the world; often abbreviated as -Attribute(s)- Check (e.g. Check)
Spell
Arcane or Supernatural Action with fantasic results.
Supernatural
Descriptor of mystical effects created by extraplanar forces.
Tandem
Term meaning to roll two Mod Dice together but only take the higher value for the Check total (e.g., / Check); shorthanded as " / ". Negative Mod Dice still subtract from the Check total.
Trained Skill Check
Skill Check made to do something that requires specific training or knowledge; requires the appropriate Hobby or Profession. Abbreviated as "'Hobby or Profession' Check".
VIG
(Stands for Vigor) Measure of a creature's health and strength.
Vitality
Resource that represents a creautres physical wellbeing and how close they are to death; a creature that reaches 0 Vitality dies.
Weakend
subtracting 1d4 from the Check Total.

fields.Evocation: Type of spell cast by borrowing power.
fields.Facet: A feature of a PC, comes from many sources.
fields.Hindered X: Modifies Checks by reducing the size of the largest Mod Die by one step for each level (e.g., from a d4 to a d2).
fields.Hobby: An activity a PC had experience in before they became an adventurer; allows a PC to make Trained Skill Checks related to them.
fields.INT: {INT} (Stands for Intelligence) Measure of how smart a creature is.
fields.Maneuver: Technique requiring great physical or mental skill.
fields.Mod Die: (Stands for Modifer Die) A die rolled with a d20 when making a Check; often shorthanded to -Attribute- Die (e.g., {VIG} Die).
fields.PER: {PER} (Stands for Perception) Measure of how well a creature utilizes its senses.
fields.PC: (Stands for Player Character) A creature controlled by one of the players during a session.
fields.PM: (Stands for Prism Master) The game master; they control everything in the story apart from PCs.
fields.Profession: A PC's occupation before they became an adventurer; allows a PC to make money during Downtime and make Trained Skill Checks related to them.
fields.PRS: {PRS} (Stands for Presence) Measure of how influential a creature is.
fields.Radiance: Resource that allows a creature to improve any Check they make by expending it.
fields.Save Check: Check made when a creature attempts to avoid something harmful.
fields.Skill Check: Check made when a creature tries to affect the world; often abbreviated as -Attribute(s)- Check (e.g. {AGI} Check)
fields.Spell: Arcane or Supernatural Action with fantasic results.
fields.Supernatural: Descriptor of mystical effects created by extraplanar forces.
fields.Tandem: Term meaning to roll two Mod Dice together but only take the higher value for the Check total (e.g., {VIG} / {AGI} Check); shorthanded as " / ". Negative Mod Dice still subtract from the Check total.
fields.Trained Skill Check: Skill Check made to do something that requires specific training or knowledge; requires the appropriate Hobby or Profession. Abbreviated as "'Hobby or Profession' Check".
fields.VIG: {VIG} (Stands for Vigor) Measure of a creature's health and strength.
fields.Vitality: Resource that represents a creautres physical wellbeing and how close they are to death; a creature that reaches 0 Vitality dies.
